title: Encryption at rest, the keystore and biometric unlock

videos.script:
Encryption on a phone protects against one kind of person. {{lost}} Somebody who has the storage and not the unlocked phone: a thief, a backup, a forensic copy. It does nothing against code running as your app, and the lesson starts by saying so.

Then three layers. {{platform}} The platform already encrypts your files under the lock screen, and you choose when they can be read. {{envelope}} Your app can add its own encryption, with two keys. The one beside the data is wrapped. The one that wraps it lives in the hardware and never comes out.

You build that in Node, change one bit of the file, and watch it refuse to open.

{{biometric}} And last, the fingerprint. A check that returns true is a curtain. A check that releases the key is a lock.
